subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw define a versioned fail-closed response-gate/plugin API for mandatory tool-call accounting and validators, and what default semantics should it have?
rationale: Current hooks cannot provide this guarantee, and choosing fail-closed delivery, validator authority, retries, fallbacks, audit records, and config shape is a product/security policy decision.

options.title: Design a versioned response gate
options.body: Create a core/plugin contract for mandatory tool ledgers, typed validators, trusted plugin authority, bounded retries, deterministic fallback, and audit records while keeping domain policy packs outside core.

options.title: Extend current finalize hooks
options.body: Evolve before_agent_finalize and delivery hooks into a stronger gate, accepting the risk of overloading advisory fail-open hooks with security semantics.

options.title: Keep policy plugins advisory
options.body: Document current hooks as best-effort filtering and tool blocking only, and defer hard response enforcement until a future security boundary is approved.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response gate
recommendation.body: Create a core/plugin contract for mandatory tool ledgers, typed validators, trusted plugin authority, bounded retries, deterministic fallback, and audit records while keeping domain policy packs outside core.

likelyOwner.reason: The open choice spans security defaults, plugin/API design, config compatibility, and final-response delivery semantics.
